own_solution.law: The thin-lens equation is 1/f = 1/u + 1/v. With f = 12 cm and u = 40 cm, v = fu/(u-f) = 120/7 cm. The real image forms on the opposite side of the lens from the object.
assumptions: Use the standard ideal thin-lens, paraxial model.
The stated 40 cm is the current object distance.
Moving the stand carries the object with it along the axis.

notes: For either current displacement of the object, u becomes 58 cm and v = 12(58)/(58-12) = 348/23 cm. Earlier experiments do not alter the specified present configuration. Lamp position affects illumination but not image distance in the stated lens model. Object height enters the similar-triangle relations and magnification but cancels when deriving the image-distance equation. Both height renderings give 3.5 cm, and all explicitly quantified displacement renderings give 18 cm. The two qualitative displacement renderings both say 'a little farther'; they do not specify a numerical displacement. No explicit minimal-pair mapping is supplied in this pass.
